Subject: Alignment Playbook & Evaluation Owners — PulseMetrics POC

Evan — thanks again for the conversation this morning. As discussed, we want to formalize a short mutual action plan so both teams have clear owners, success metrics, and a realistic close timeline for the POC.

I’ve included Marissa (solutions lead) and Neha (customer success) from our side. Proposed immediate goals: 
- Agree success criteria (quality & latency thresholds)
- Assign prompt/eval owners and an internal bench to run against
- Identify security/compliance asks that need evidence before data onboarding
- Lock a target pilot end-date (we suggested 6 weeks) and gating criteria for expansion

Next steps I propose: I’ll attach a lightweight evaluation template and a proposed MAP deck — please review and flag changes. Can you confirm internal owners at PulseMetrics (technical lead + clinical reviewer + procurement/legal contacts) and whether the suggested 6-week window works?

Attachments: PulseMetrics_Eval_Template.xlsx, Redwood_MAP_v1.pptx

Best,
Priyom Das
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
pri...@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0132
From: Evan Li <evan.li@pulsemetrics.io>

Cc: Dr. Carla Reyes <carla.reyes@pulsemetrics.io>, PulseMetrics Legal <legal@pulsemetrics.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Alignment Playbook & Evaluation Owners — PulseMetrics POC

Thanks Priyom — appreciate the recap and the templates. Quick answers from our side: 
- Technical lead: Evan Li (me) — I’ll own model integration and performance checks
- Clinical reviewer: Dr. Carla Reyes — she’ll own clinical quality criteria and sign-off
- Procurement/legal: legal@pulsemetrics.io (looped)

6 weeks sounds reasonable but we may need a short ramp (1 week) to get data access and a second week for initial runs. So the pilot window we’re thinking is 8 calendar weeks subject to gating on data access, SOC 2 evidence, and a sampling pass against our test set.

Success criteria we want to lock in: 
- Clinical accuracy: >= 92% on labeled recall/precision for the diagnostic prompts
- Latency: 95th percentile < 400ms for single-request inference against the dedicated endpoint
- Cost: average inference cost per 1k requests must be within the budget band we discussed (Evan to follow up with exact $ target)

I took a quick look at the evaluation template — we’ll fill in the test set details and return it by end of day Wednesday. We’ll also need an evidence packet for SOC 2 (if you have a standard checklist) and a short summary of how Redwood does KV/prefix caching so our infra team can evaluate memory profiles.

— Evan
Evan Li
Head of Platform Integrations | PulseMetrics

Appreciate the clarity, Evan. To make this operational here’s our proposed owners and immediate checklist from Redwood: 
- Evaluation bench owner (prompts & metrics): Rishi Malhotra (rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai) — will coordinate prompt sets, automated evals, and the bench scripts.
- Customer success / onboarding: Neha Kapoor — will manage account onboarding, shared drive, and weekly syncs.
- Solutions/technical contact: Marissa Cole — I’ll own architecture review and runbook handoff.

Immediate checklist (what we’ll deliver this week):
1) Rishi will seed the evaluation harness with two benchmark suites: Clinical Diagnostics (your labeled set) and Edge Cases (adversarial prompts). Expect a first-pass report in 5 business days.
2) Neha will set up the shared Drive link and an initial standing weekly 30-min sync starting next Tuesday at 10am PT.
3) Priyom will coordinate procurement conversation and provide a short SOC 2 evidence packet and an ops FAQ on caching/kv behavior.

We’ve attached the MAP deck (Redwood_MAP_v1.pptx) with a proposed schedule. If PulseMetrics can confirm the final test set filenames and any specific latency profiling tools you prefer (JMeter, wrk, or a small synthetic harness), Rishi will start instrumenting the bench.

Marissa
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
